hook.line: Don Hernando swears you promised him a free tinto. You don't remember promising it, and you don't remember Vale promising it either. Spanish builds those two sentences differently, depending on whose action it was.

examples.es: No recuerdo que él dijera eso.
examples.en: I don't remember him saying that.

examples.es: No recuerdo haber firmado ese contrato.
examples.en: I don't remember signing that contract.

examples.es: No recuerdo que Vale firmara ese contrato.
examples.en: I don't remember Vale signing that contract.

examples.es: No recuerdo que nos dijeran nada.
examples.en: I don't remember them telling us anything.

rule:
Ask yourself one question: who did the thing I am trying to remember?

It was me: *No recuerdo haber dicho eso.* *Haber* + the *-do* form of the verb (*dicho*, *firmado*, *llamado*). English "remember saying" works the same way.

It was someone else: *No recuerdo que él dijera eso.* *Que* + the past *-ra* form (*dijera*, *firmara*, *dijeran*).

English uses "him saying" for the second and gives no clue about the verb change. In Spanish, the shape tells you whose action it was.
smallPrint: Teachers call this same subject versus different subject: one subject gives an infinitive, two subjects give *que* plus the subjunctive.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *No recuerdo ___ ese contrato.* (*haber firmado* or *que firmara*) I don't remember signing that contract.
yourTurn.answer: No recuerdo haber firmado ese contrato.
yourTurn.why: I did the signing, so there is one subject and the infinitive fits.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *No recuerdo ___ ese contrato.* (*haber firmado* or *que firmara*) I don't remember Vale signing that contract.
yourTurn.answer: No recuerdo que Vale firmara ese contrato.
yourTurn.why: Vale did the signing, so a second subject needs *que* plus the past form.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I don't remember saying that.
accept: No me acuerdo de haber dicho eso.
yourTurn.why: Same person remembering and doing: *haber* plus *dicho*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I don't remember him saying that.
yourTurn.answer: No recuerdo que él dijera eso.
accept: No me acuerdo de que él dijera eso.
yourTurn.why: A different person did it, so *que* plus *dijera*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Do you (informal) remember calling Mariana?
accept: ¿Te acuerdas de haber llamado a Mariana?
yourTurn.why: You are asking about the listener's own action, so the infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about Tomás: *No recuerdo haber llegado tarde.* (I don't remember Tomás arriving late.)
yourTurn.answer: No recuerdo que Tomás llegara tarde.
yourTurn.why: A new person arrives, so the sentence switches to *que* plus *llegara*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I don't remember them telling us anything.
yourTurn.answer: No recuerdo que nos dijeran nada.
accept: No me acuerdo de que nos dijeran nada.
yourTurn.why: *Ellos* is the other subject, so *que* plus the plural *dijeran*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. When you are the one who acted, Spanish wants *haber* plus *dicho*.

pitfalls.wrong: No recuerdo que él dijo eso.
pitfalls.right: No recuerdo que él dijera eso.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After a negative *no recuerdo que*, the next verb takes the past *-ra* form.

pitfalls.wrong: No recuerdo de haber dicho eso.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Recordar* takes its infinitive directly, with no *de*.

personal: Think of something someone says you did. Say that you do not remember it with *No recuerdo haber…*, then say you do not remember a friend doing something with *No recuerdo que…*.
